transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Recording ID: fireflies-20261105-crestfield-01
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Carlos Diaz (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Head of Compliance, Crestfield), Tom Liu (CTO, Crestfield), Evan Ross (Security Engineer, Crestfield)

Summary:
Short: Discovery focused on Crestfield Bank's requirements for data residency, GDPR and financial-services controls, and logging limitations. Customer interested in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options; key constraints are EU data residency for EU customers, strict audit logs retention policies, and restrictions on storing PII in logs. Redwood AE/SE committed to share SOC2/ISO artifacts, a dedicated deployment diagram, and schedule an SE deep dive.

Topics:
- Data residency (regional isolation, EU/US boundaries)
- Compliance: GDPR, GLBA controls, HIPAA possibility for certain lines, SOC2/ISO expectations
- Logging and telemetry: retention, redaction, PII in logs, ability to disable request/response logging
- Deployment options: Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC/on-prem)
- KMS and key management, HSM, customer-managed keys
- Audit logs, RBAC, SSO/SAML, and contractual SLAs

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE. With me is Carlos, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:08] Asha: Good, thanks. I'm Asha. We just want to get straight into data residency and logging constraints for our digital banking features.
[00:15] Tom: Yeah hi, Tom here. We already use a few managed ML services so want to see where Redwood fits for infra and compliance.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Quick agenda - we'll run through your requirements, show how Redwood's Hosted/Dedicated/Private options map to those, and Carlos can talk technical specifics. Then next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Tom: Perfect.
[00:32] Carlos: Thanks, quick note - if at any time you want deep-dive perf numbers we can set up a dedicated benchmark session.
[00:38] Asha: Good. First question: for EU customers, we need all data to remain in the EU. We can't have any PII leave the region. How does Redwood handle that?
[00:48] Maya: Sure, two parts - logical data residency and physical. For Hosted we offer region-scoped endpoints, so requests can be routed to EU regions only. For Dedicated you can reserve capacity in EU regions and get stronger tenancy isolation. For strict regulatory needs we recommend Private (VPC or on-prem) where the control plane can be customer-managed and egress is controlled.
[01:10] Evan: When you say Hosted, is data ever replicated to US for analytics or backups?
[01:16] Carlos: By default we keep customer data and logs in-region. Backups follow region policy - for Hosted we can provide contract language to ensure EU-only backups. If you need guaranteed no replication outside EU, Private is the safest.
[01:28] Asha: Okay. Next - logging. We cannot have request/response payloads containing customer PII in your logs. Can we disable request/response logging completely and still get operational metrics?
[01:39] Maya: Yes, you can opt out of request/response logging. We offer token-level metrics, latency, error rates without retaining payloads. For Dedicated and Private deployments you can also configure log redaction and disable payload capture.
[01:52] Tom: And for audit requirements, we need immutable audit logs showing who accessed model configs and when. Retention for 7 years for some records. Can Redwood provide that?
[02:03] Carlos: We support audit logs with append-only storage and export to customer S3 or logging endpoints. Retention policies can be configured; for Hosted we can retain longer but for multi-year retention we typically recommend Dedicated with exported logs to your own archive.
[02:18] Asha: Do you support integration with our SIEM - Splunk and a Kafka pipeline?
[02:23] Carlos: Yes, we'll push audit events to your SIEM via HTTPS or to an S3 bucket that your pipeline ingests. We also support Kafka in Private deployments.
[02:33] Evan: Encryption keys - can we bring our own KMS keys (BYOK)?
[02:38] Maya: Yes, BYOK is supported in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys backed by cloud KMS in some regions; we can discuss HSM-backed keys for higher assurance.
[02:49] Tom: For HIPAA - some of our small business banking products may fall under PHI handling. Is Redwood HIPAA-friendly?
[02:56] Carlos: We have customers running HIPAA workloads; typically that requires a Private deployment and a BAA. We'll need to review the specific data flows but yes, Private with customer-managed keys and audit exports is the standard path.
[03:10] Asha: GDPR data subject requests - we need the ability to delete user data if requested. Does Redwood have delete-by-PII workflows and proof of deletion?
[03:20] Maya: We provide APIs for data deletion and can emit deletion events. For Hosted we log deletion actions in audit logs; for Dedicated/Private you can run tools to confirm removal from caches and storage. We can provide a deletion certification process as part of contract.
[03:33] Evan: About telemetry - are there any default debug traces that might contain full prompts? We've seen other vendors accidentally log prompts in trace output.
[03:42] Carlos: Good callout. By default we do not log full prompts in high-fidelity traces for production customers. Tracing is configurable and can be limited to identifiers and token counts. For any debug sessions we recommend explicit opt-in and time-boxed capture.
[03:57] Asha: What about model card data - who has access to model weights or fine-tuning artifacts?
[04:03] Maya: Customers own their fine-tunes. For open model variants we provide curated model binaries; only infra team in our cloud has access to the underlying artifacts for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private, artifacts live in your environment.
[04:16] Tom: Network isolation - can we whitelabel IP ranges or restrict egress so that models can't call out?
[04:23] Carlos: Yes, in Private deployments you control egress. In Dedicated we provide IP allowlists and VPC peering options. Hosted supports strict IP filtering and region-based routing but full egress control is best in Private.
[04:37] Asha: Let's talk breach notification timelines. We need 24/48 hour notification SLA for incidents impacting data residency or unauthorized access.
[04:46] Maya: Our standard incident response is 72 hours for public notification but for enterprise contracts we can negotiate 24/48 hour notification windows and dedicated SIRT contact points.
[04:58] Evan: On logging retention, some regs say no logs can exist that contain certain data longer than 30 days. Can we set per-log-type retention?
[05:06] Carlos: Yes. Retention is configurable by log type. Event and audit logs can be kept long-term; request payload logs can be set to zero retention. We'll add a policy matrix to show defaults and configurable options.
[05:19] Asha: Do you have a SOC2 Type II? We need to see reports and potentially have a security review team meet.
[05:24] Maya: Yes we do SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 - I'll share the artifacts after an NDA. We can also set up a security intake with our security team next week.
[05:34] Tom: Cost - quick note: we need unit economics estimates. For Dedicated, how granular is billing? Per GPU-hour, per token?
[05:42] Carlos: Dedicated is typically committed capacity (monthly) with cost per GPU-hour and per-token for overage. For Hosted it's per-token. We'll share a pricing sheet reflecting reserved pools and burst policies.
[05:53] Asha: One more - contractually we need clause ensuring logs with PII are never used for model training, and that Redwood won't use customer data to improve public models.
[06:03] Maya: Absolutely - we can include a clause prohibiting training on customer data and ensure data is used only for serving, not for Redwood model training. For Hosted we'd codify that in our DPA and contract.
[06:14] Evan: For the pilot we'd like an initial dedicated pool scoped to EU region, small size (1-2 GPUs) to validate latency and log behavior. Can you support that?
[06:23] Carlos: Yes, we can provision a small dedicated pool for pilot, scoped regionally, and run synthetic and replayed traffic. We'll need your sample traffic or representative prompts.
[06:32] Tom: About timelines - we aim to have a pilot started within 3 weeks and production in 3 months if all goes well. Is that realistic?
[06:40] Maya: That aligns - pilot in 2-3 weeks depending on contract and access; production in 8-12 weeks typical for Dedicated/Private depending on procurement.
[06:50] Asha: Any red flags we should be aware of when comparing Hosted vs Dedicated for compliance?
[06:56] Carlos: Hosted is the easiest to start but has the least control; Dedicated gives tenancy isolation and better audit/export controls; Private gives the most control and is recommended for highest assurance or HIPAA. If your controls require customer-managed keys and no cross-region replication, Private is the conservative choice.
[07:10] Maya: To be actionable - we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, a Dedicated and Private deployment diagram, and a pilot pricing estimate. Carlos will set up a technical deep dive to review VPC connectivity and benchmark plan.
[07:23] Evan: We'll provide allowed IP ranges and a sample data flow diagram.
[07:28] Tom: Also we'd like to vet your legal DPA language around data residency and training prohibition.
[07:33] Maya: Understood, legal will follow up.
[07:36] Asha: One last quick operational question - rate limiting and telemetry sampling, can we tune that so that logs used for billing do not inadvertently capture PII?
[07:46] Carlos: Yes - telemetry sampling and rate limiting are configurable per-route. Billing metrics are token counts, not full prompt storage.
[07:53] Asha: Great. Thanks, that's most of our questions.
[07:56] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll send over the artifacts tomorrow and follow up with the deep dive invite.
[08:02] Tom: Appreciate it.
[08:04] Evan: Thanks.
